values.note: $20 a site, tent or RV, on recreation.gov's 2026 and 2027 tables and the NPS record. The park entrance pass is required and not included in the camping fee.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234685/rates (Peak RV NONELECTRIC 20, TENT ONLY NONELECTRIC 20; 2026 and 2027) + https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=grsa (fees 'Individual Site, Per Night' 20.00) + recreation.gov notice ('An entrance pass is required while in the park and is not included in the camping fee'), read 2026-10-27

hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234685 (notice 'No showers, hookups or laundry facilities available in the park') + NPS record (electricalHookups 0), read 2026-10-27

values.note: 88 sites in Loops 1 and 2 (52 RV, 34 tent-only) plus 3 tent-only group sites. RV, or vehicle plus trailer, limited to 35 ft combined; the NPS says 'RVs or trailers up to 33 feet may fit in a few sites'. Most sites are small and unlevel: per-site lengths on recreation.gov run 15-35 ft, 28 of the 54 RV-usable sites at 25 ft or more. Mostly back-in or parallel, 2 pull-throughs. If the rig is longer than the site booked there is no alternative site.

sites.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234685 ('The campground offers 88 campsites'; 'Total combined length limit is 35 feet. RVs over 35 feet, or combined vehicle plus trailer length over 35 feet, are not allowed'; 'Most sites are small and unlevel') + per-site catalog (Max Vehicle Length 20 x20, 25 x19, 30 x7, 35 x2 among RV-usable sites; Driveway Entry Back-in 40, Parallel 12, Pull-through 2) + https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=grsa (rvInfo, rvMaxLength 33, trailerMaxLength 20), read 2026-10-27

values.note: All seasonal. Restrooms with sinks and a dishwashing basin; bear boxes; firewood and ice sold in summer. Limited cell signal; nearest wifi in Alamosa.

facilities.source: https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=grsa (amenities: toilets 'Flush Toilets - seasonal', potableWater 'Yes - seasonal', dumpStation 'Yes - seasonal', campStore 'Yes - seasonal', showers 'None', laundry 'No', internetConnectivity 'No') + recreation.gov notice ('No showers, hookups or laundry facilities'), read 2026-10-27

season.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsa/planyourvisit/camping.htm ('The campground is open April 1st through October 31st each year') + NPS record ('Open April through October, closed November through March'), read 2026-10-27

values.note: Reservation required for every site, on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777, up to 3 months ahead (shortened from 6 months for 2026 while the campground is improved); no first-come camping, no waiting list. Reservable 'Peak Season' 2027: April 1 - October 30. Pick a site that fits the rig - there is no alternative site if it doesn't. 8 people, 2 vehicles per site (a trailer counts).

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234685 (rules reservationWindow 3 Months; notices 'You must have a reservation ... First-come, first-serve camping is not available', 'There is no waiting list') + /rates (Peak Season 2027-04-01 to 2027-10-30) + https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/alerts?parkCode=grsa ('sites can be reserved 3 months in advance beginning in 2026') + NPS record (reservationInfo 'All sites are by reservation only through recreation.gov 1-877-444-6777'), read 2026-10-27

note: Great Sand Dunes NP & Preserve campground among piñon pines and sagebrush a mile north of the visitor center, with views of the dunefield and the Sangre de Cristo peaks. Paved, historic-design loops. Generators only 8-10 a.m., noon-2 p.m. and 5-7 p.m. Medano Creek at the foot of the dunes runs in late spring and summer. --Claude
